regions.name: The Hald Valley
regions.terrain: valley, a closed upland river valley under the range
regions.notes: Held by: The Haldren. Other small dale peoples beyond the ridges.

regions.name: The Folddales
regions.terrain: hill, upland cut into closed river valleys
regions.water: many small rivers running east to the Haldwater; low wet ground on the east
regions.notes: Held by: Small dale peoples, a few hundred to a valley, each shut from the next. Unheld as a whole.

regions.name: The High Scarrow
regions.terrain: mountain, snow peaks and fir slopes
regions.water: snowfields; short streams east and west
regions.notes: Held by: The pass folk on the heights. Unheld below.

regions.name: The Deep Scarrow
regions.terrain: mountain, the heart of the range, high closed valleys
regions.notes: Held by: The pass folk.

regions.name: The Low Scarrow
regions.terrain: mountain, the range falling south, forested
regions.water: streams to the Withy and the Sarn
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; charcoal burners and hill villages on the south side sell grain to Quillan.

regions.name: The Underfell
regions.terrain: valley, a high valley at the mountain foot with one way in
regions.notes: Held by: The Hodd.

regions.name: The Corrow Hills
regions.terrain: hill, steep wooded hills at the range end
regions.water: short streams north to the sea
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; woodcutters and fog.

regions.name: The Sennway
regions.terrain: hill, the gap in the northern hills
regions.notes: Held by: The Senn.

regions.name: The Corrant Strand
regions.terrain: coast, northern lowland and shore
regions.notes: Held by: The Corrant.

regions.name: The Greyspur
regions.terrain: hill, a grey stony spur and its dales
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; shepherds who answer to no one. The Tavrek use its east end.

regions.name: The Hollow March
regions.terrain: hill, empty foreland between the dales and the rim
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; a few herders. Half-walked country.

regions.name: The North Ashring
regions.terrain: hill, worn bare hills ringing the basin, north half
regions.notes: Held by: The people of the rim.

regions.name: The South Ashring
regions.terrain: hill, worn bare hills ringing the basin, south half
regions.notes: Held by: The people of the rim.

regions.name: The Bare Floor
regions.terrain: plain, a pale bare shallow basin
regions.notes: Held by: No one. No one goes down.

regions.name: The Rivermeet
regions.terrain: plain, grass and water meadow where the rivers gather
regions.water: the Lowe, the Hornwater, the Longloop
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; scattered farm villages that pay no crown.

regions.name: The Hornfoot Grass
regions.terrain: steppe, grass under the spur and along the north shore
regions.water: the Hornwater and the Longloop rise here
regions.notes: Held by: The Tavrek.

regions.name: The Windward Grass
regions.terrain: steppe, open grass to the north-east shore
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; the Tavrek hunt it in summer.

regions.name: The Tern Shore
regions.terrain: coast, low stony hills and a cold bay
regions.notes: Held by: A few fishing hamlets.

regions.name: The Noman Grass
regions.terrain: steppe, the wide middle grass
regions.water: the Lowe along its western side; the Dunwater
regions.notes: Held by: No one.

regions.name: The Rope Ridges
regions.terrain: hill, long parallel grass ridges
regions.water: the Ropewater between the ridge lines
regions.notes: Held by: The Ushkai.

regions.name: The Thornhollows
regions.terrain: steppe, the grass southern edge, thorn and sheltered hollows
regions.water: winter pools; the Pellwater on the south
regions.notes: Held by: The Ushkai in winter; free farms along the Pellwater.

regions.name: The Parting Woods
regions.terrain: forest, wooded lowland where the great river divides
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; woodsmen, and free farms that sell grain down both rivers.

regions.name: The Pell Mouth
regions.terrain: coast, estuary, dyked ground and tidal flats
regions.notes: Held by: The Pellim.

regions.name: The Saltmarket Plain
regions.terrain: plain, farmed lowland behind the drowned coast
regions.notes: Held by: The Thessend (the crown of Talcross).

regions.name: The Crownlands
regions.terrain: plain, farmed lowland on the lower great river
regions.water: the lower Lowe and the Withy mouth
regions.notes: Held by: The Thessend (the crowns of Vessany and Ardmoor).

regions.name: The Middle Reach
regions.terrain: valley, the great river middle course, terraces and water meadow
regions.notes: Held by: The Loweth, who pay a due to Vessany.

regions.name: The Reedsea
regions.terrain: marsh, the great delta marsh
regions.notes: Held by: The reed folk.

regions.name: The Withywood
regions.terrain: forest, wide lowland forest, oak and beech
regions.notes: Held by: Unheld; woodsmen, charcoal burners, a few clearings.

regions.name: The Bendlands
regions.terrain: hill, low wooded hills and bottomland on a looping river
regions.climate: mild temperate, winters that keep people in
regions.notes: Held by: The Brannow, and free farms upriver.

regions.name: The Far Capes
regions.terrain: hill, wooded capes and cliff shore
regions.notes: Held by: No one; a few coast fishers.

regions.name: The Grey Reach
regions.terrain: sea, a cold northern sea

regions.name: The Sundown Sea
regions.terrain: sea, a narrow sea under cliffs

regions.name: The Southern Deep
regions.terrain: sea, the broad southern and south-western sea

regions.name: The Drowned Shelf
regions.terrain: sea, a pale shallow shelf with islands and flats

features.name: Ostrey
features.known_to: the Haldren; the dale peoples; salt carters
features.notes: The Haldren town above the stepping stones. About 300.

features.name: The Haldwater
features.notes: Upper course of the great river. Cold and quick in the valley, slow through the wet ground.

features.name: The Lowe
features.known_to: everyone on it; the south knows it best
features.notes: The long river. Braided above the Parting, navigable from the Rivermeet down.

features.name: The Fitted Way
features.known_to: the Haldren, as a line of fitted stone under the turf
features.notes: An Orsand road, under turf for most of its length.

features.name: The Wetfoot
features.known_to: the dale peoples; carters on the Salt Road
features.notes: Low wet ground where the dale rivers leave the hills.

features.name: The Highfold
features.notes: Roofless stone folds and a walled platform on the high ground above Ostrey, where the Haldren leave their dead.

features.name: The Knot Stair
features.known_to: the pass folk; a few Haldren by repute
features.notes: High pass at the head of the Hald Valley. Kept by the pass folk.

features.name: The Kettle
features.known_to: the pass folk, who watch it
features.notes: A high rock hollow with an overhang on its north side. The warm stone lies on its floor.

features.name: The High Way
features.known_to: the pass folk; no lowlander walks it whole
features.notes: The Fitted Way continued over the range to the western shore. Broken by slides.

features.name: Westerhythe
features.known_to: the pass folk; coasting boats see it
features.notes: An Orsand harbor under the western cliffs: a mole, a stair, a holed sighting stone on the cliff top.

features.name: The Marchway
features.notes: The Fitted Way continued east to the rim.

features.name: The Withy
features.notes: Rises under the Kettle, runs the trough between range and rim, then through the great wood to the Lowe.

features.name: Undercrag
features.notes: The Hodd walled seat. About 3,600 inside.

features.name: The Squared Doors
features.known_to: the Hodd; the pass folk, whose they are
features.notes: Squared openings in the cliff above the terraces: pass-folk cut rooms, some in use.

features.name: The Lintel Door
features.known_to: the Hodd, as a blocked doorway; the pass folk
features.notes: A doorway of dressed stone high on the slope, blocked with fitted blocks from outside. An Orsand sealed room.

features.name: The Hush
features.known_to: the pass folk; Hodd goatherds, by avoiding it
features.notes: A high hollow and a deep cut room closed from outside. Nothing particular grows in the hollow.

features.name: Kinhold
features.notes: The largest of the pass-folk winter houses, cut inside the mountain.

features.name: Dunmarrow
features.known_to: the Senn; the Corrant; everyone who uses the Salt Road
features.notes: The Senn walled town at the crossing. Two gates.

features.name: The Bare Gate
features.notes: Two tall dressed stones either side of the road on open ground, with no wall.

features.name: The Corra
features.notes: Cold and quick in the gap, slow below it.

features.name: Gullwick
features.notes: Port city of the Corrant at the mouth of the Corra. About 8,000. Built on an older harbor.

features.name: Panmouth
features.notes: Chief town of the north-shore salt pans.

features.name: The Salt Road
features.notes: In use from Gullwick to the Wetfoot; beyond that an old road only.

features.name: Old Orsa
features.known_to: the rim people, who take its stone; Thessend scribes, from records
features.notes: Chief ruin of the road-making kingdom, on the north rim. Ruins over older ruins.

features.name: The Holed Stone
features.notes: A leaning slab with a hole bored through it, on the crest above Old Orsa, looking in over the basin.

features.name: The Measure House
features.notes: A sealed vault under Old Orsa. The lowest of the Orsand doors.

features.name: The Sleeper
features.known_to: the rim people; anyone on the rim crest
features.notes: The beast at the middle of the basin. The painted mound is the beast and the rise it lies on.

features.name: Goatsteps
features.known_to: the rim people; salt carters from the Lowe
features.notes: The rim hamlet nearest the river, where outsiders trade salt for goats.

features.name: The Rib
features.notes: A long pale curve standing out of the turf on the spur east hillside, with a hollow under it.

features.name: The Twin Spring
features.notes: A wet saddle of springs under the spur from which two rivers run opposite ways.

features.name: The Hornwater
features.notes: Runs west from the Twin Spring to the Lowe.

features.name: The Longloop
features.notes: Runs east and then south-west in a great loop from the Twin Spring to the Lowe.

features.name: The Dunwater
features.notes: A steppe stream from the middle grass to the Longloop.

features.name: The Ropewater
features.notes: Runs west between the ridge lines, then south-west to the Lowe.

features.name: The Hardway
features.known_to: the Tavrek, as a straight stretch of thin grass
features.notes: An Orsand road along the north grass to the Tern Shore.

features.name: The Rope Line
features.known_to: the Ushkai, as the lines where the sky dragged its rope
features.notes: An Orsand road from the rim across the ridges and off the sheet.

features.name: The Flat Banks
features.notes: Banks and ditches worn nearly flat in a hollow, enclosing nothing: an Orsand road station.

features.name: Lastlight
features.notes: A fishing hamlet on the Tern Shore that keeps a fire on an old stone tower every night.

features.name: The Sunder
features.notes: The east arm of the Lowe, from the Parting to the Pellwater. A chain of pools in a dry summer.

features.name: The Pellwater
features.known_to: the Pellim; the Ushkai on its upper course
features.notes: Comes in from the east along the grass edge and reaches the sea through the estuary.

features.name: Saltstairs
features.known_to: the whole south and every coast
features.notes: The Pellim city on the tide. About 20,000.

features.name: The Dry Hull
features.notes: Ribs of a large old hull on dry ground, well back from the shore.

features.name: The Tide Stumps
features.notes: Lines of worked stone and pile stumps on the flats at low water: the lower old harbor.

features.name: Kessary
features.notes: The Loweth walled seat and landing, on the footings of a river fort.

features.name: The Bankwater
features.notes: A wide still water in a side valley above Kessary, held behind a straight bank.

features.name: Sellnot
features.known_to: the Loweth, as a tale; Crownlands records
features.notes: The town drowned under the Bankwater.

features.name: The Springdoor
features.notes: A sealed Orsand door beside the old spring of Sellnot, under the Bankwater.

features.name: Wardwell
features.notes: A spring cased in old dressed stone on the hillside above Kessary.

features.name: The Stopped Road
features.notes: An Orsand road from the south rim that comes down to the river at Kessary and stops.

features.name: Vessany
features.notes: The upriver crown of the Thessend. About 8,000.

features.name: Ardmoor
features.notes: The middle crown of the Thessend. About 6,000.

features.name: Talcross
features.notes: The coastal crown of the Thessend, the lowest and oldest. About 9,000.

features.name: The Drowned Streets
features.notes: Worked stone running out under the marsh water, under the oldest reed-folk villages.

features.name: The Eastflat
features.known_to: the reed folk; Ardmoor eel buyers
features.notes: The east reach of the marsh: wide, shallow, one kind of reed, no eels.

features.name: Quillan
features.notes: The Brannow walled town on the rise in the great bend. About 6,500 inside.

features.name: The Sarn
features.notes: A slow full river with one great bend.

features.name: The Underkeys
features.notes: Fitted doors at the ends of the cellars of Quillan oldest quarter. Orsand sealed rooms.

features.name: The Bottom Mounds
features.notes: Regular mounds in the bottomland with trees grown over them.

features.name: The Banked Way
features.known_to: the Brannow, as old banked roads into the woods
features.notes: An Orsand road from the bend town north-east through the great wood to the rim.

features.name: The Edder
features.notes: A forest river to the southern sea.

features.name: The Lamp Hut
features.known_to: no one living; a few coast fishers know a hut stands there
features.notes: A stone hut and a fire platform on a cape. A carved lintel.

features.name: The Stairfoot Door
features.notes: A sealed Orsand room cut under the Knot Stair, beside the old road.

features.name: Lakewall
features.known_to: the rim people, as stumps on the floor seen from above
features.notes: Stumps of walls and a quay with no water, on the old shore line of the basin. First-age work.

features.name: Tollmere
features.known_to: the farm villages of the Rivermeet
features.notes: Grassed mounds and a burned layer on the bank of the Lowe: a market city of the broken provinces.

features.name: Emberholt
features.notes: An Orsand provincial town gone to forest, on the Banked Way.

features.name: Stonemeet
features.known_to: herders of both peoples, as a place of dry wells
features.notes: A caravan town on the Rope Line, abandoned when its wells went flat.

features.name: The Leaving Stone
features.notes: A flat stone beside the old road thirty miles above Ostrey, where goods are left by night for the people of the heights.

features.name: The Night Table
features.notes: A flat stone above the terraces of Undercrag where the silent trade is done.
